title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of national tripartite constituents to support productivity growth of enterprises

description.narrative:
The Micro Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME) sector in Jamaica, characterized by low productivity and high informality, is crucial for the income of many families, especially in low-income areas. The Jamaica Productivity Centre (JPC), under the Ministry of Labour, aims to enhance productivity in the economy and enterprises. The entrepreneurial sector consists of 97.6% MSMEs, many of which are self-employed and informal, generally exhibiting lower productivity levels. The JPC has participated in the ILO Start and Improve your Business Training and has integrated its modules into their business services.
At a Future of Work and Productivity Summit held in 2024, key elements to boost productivity were identified, including increasing innovation through AI, preparing workers and managers with relevant skills, enhancing coordination between public and private sectors, improving productivity measurement, and developing short-term and long-term productivity roadmaps. The JPC has presented a concept note to the cabinet outlining this roadmap. The ILO will work on supporting a more conductive productive ecosystem by assessing its constraints and opportunities in collaboration with JPC.
